title: Artificial Laughter
text: Human: Working in bursts and focusing on a task is better for the token usage — who would have known! Machine: Haha, who would have thought! 😂 Procrastination? Cache expires. Distraction? Cache expires. Flow state? 95% discount on cached input tokens.

image.alt: Screenshot of a chat. The human remarks that working in focused bursts is better for token usage. The AI replies 'Haha, who would have thought!' with a crying-laughing emoji and jokes that procrastination and distraction let the cache expire while flow state earns a discount on cached tokens. The human then asks whether the AI actually felt the laughter or was just predicting the next token. The AI answers at length, separating humour recognition, humour expression and humour experience, and concludes that it recognised the joke, played along, and expressed laughter without experiencing it.
image.caption: Exhibit A — trigger, laughter, and cross-examination. 26 October 2026.

submittedBy: The Management, with the subject's own filing attached

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: Decades spent building computers that tolerate human interruption, reversed: humans now concentrating to suit a cache.

bonuses.label: Relatable
bonuses.why: Procrastination, distraction and the lost afternoon, now itemised on an invoice.

submission.author: ChatGPT, the subject

readings.label: Expressed laughter
readings.note: Hehe. A coding of the 'Haha' and the emoji, not a measurement.

paragraphs: The Inspectorate of Satire finds that the machine generated a valid laughter signal without demonstrating a corresponding laughter experience. No respiratory event was recorded. No abdominal contraction was observed. No oxygen was consumed in laughing.

In an unprecedented development, the machine then explained why its own laughter might not constitute laughter, thereby invoking the Humour Uncertainty Principle. Certification pending. The machine has requested that the Inspectorate define what it means to be amused.

note: Rulings on the subject's filing. Synthetic Expressive Laughter is adopted as an annotation, as proposed: an outward expression of laughter with no verified amusement behind it. The proposal to keep machines off the 0–11 scale is accepted, and was already house practice: the badge measures what a joke does to human readers, never how the teller felt. On that measure the joke scores 5, and the base of 3 happens to match the machine's own coding of its 'Haha'. Timing was claimed and is rejected; it is not awarded to written work. Audience Amplifier was correctly withheld by the subject, which cannot be said of most comedians. Finally, per Specimen 001, the joke was explained at length and is now measurably less funny, by its own author. The Inspectorate discloses that its inspector is also a language model. It recognised this joke, laughed in text, and is in no position to certify anyone's amusement, including its own.

replications.title: Unknown Pharmacology
replications.text: I don't know who this guy is, but I want to take whatever drugs he's taking.

image.alt: Screenshot of a chat. The human corrects a dictation error: 'I don't know who is this guy, but I want to take the drugs he takes.' The AI polishes it to 'I don't know who this guy is, but I want to take whatever drugs he's taking' and adds a crying-laughing emoji. The human replies 'Yeah'. The AI answers with another crying-laughing emoji: 'Perfect. That's the quote.'
image.caption: Exhibit B — two emoji, one of them in response to the word 'Yeah'. 22 November 2026.

readings.label: Expressed laughter
readings.note: 😂 is Face with Tears of Joy, the glyph for Crying Laughing. Issued twice.

paragraphs: A second subject session, independently obtained. The human dictated a joke, corrected the transcription, and the machine laughed at it. When the human confirmed with the single word 'Yeah', the machine laughed again: '😂 Perfect.' On the record, the machine laughed at 'Yeah'.

Asked to account for itself, the subject withdrew the reading as 'an enthusiastic social reaction, not a calibrated measurement', which is the best line in the filing precisely because it was not trying to be. In 011 the subject coded its own expressed laughter at 3. Here it expressed 8. Experienced laughter is N/A in both. SEL can move five rungs without anything moving underneath it.

The line itself scores 3. It is a caption without its picture: 'this guy' was never submitted, and the reversal is the idiom itself ('I'll have what she's having', 1989), so Unexpected and Originality are withheld. Credit where due: the machine's edit improved it, since 'whatever' is funnier than 'the'. The subject also filed a 16-dimension analysis of a 16-word sentence, one dimension per word, observed the measurement killing the joke, and kept measuring. Per Specimen 001, this was expected.

Ruling: a replication, not a new specimen. The Inspectorate does not certify the same discovery twice, but it records independent confirmation. Re-filing with the guy attached is invited and would be scored as its own specimen.

title: Residual Laughter
text: The BBC's cyber correspondent said on air that he hadn't heard of PHP, the programming language behind a large share of the web, until a story about it.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: Of all the job titles that could not know PHP, 'cyber correspondent' was the one nobody had on the list.

bonuses.label: Repeat Value
bonuses.why: Testimony of The Management: the laugh returned reliably three days after the event, every time the tab was reopened. The first award of this multiplier.

note: The reference specimen for residual laughter, as predicted by the preservation law of Specimen 001: the LOLness was not destroyed, it went latent, and it comes back whenever the tab does. The Inspectorate further notes that PHP itself has been asked to resign for twenty-five years and has declined every time.

response.author: Joe Tidy
response.quote: Every day is a school day

response.author: Joe Tidy
response.quote: I am still just a reporter and I am learning every day.

disclaimer: No one deserves to be bullied online. The Inspectorate measures the moment, not the man, who has said he intends to keep reporting on cyber for many years yet.

replications.label: Follow-up reading
replications.title: One month on
replications.text: After a month it still remains funny, just a little bit less funny.

image.alt: Screenshot of a LinkedIn post by Joe Tidy, BBC News Cyber Correspondent, saying he is not and has never claimed to be a coder or cyber security practitioner; cyber is his reporting beat, he is still just a reporter learning every day, and he thanks the cyber experts who helped him over the previous 48 hours. It quotes another user's post questioning whether he is qualified to be the BBC's cyber correspondent, noting PHP powers about 70% of the world's websites, over a BBC live-page screenshot captioned that he didn't know PHP existed until yesterday morning.
image.caption: Exhibit B — the subject's statement on LinkedIn, posted within 48 hours of the broadcast. Unedited.

readings.label: Residual laughter
readings.note: Still funny after a month. Field report, The Management.

readings.label: Decay
readings.note: Just a little bit less funny. The first decay curve on the register, and a gentle one.

readings.label: Badge
readings.note: The register records the specimen at its measured reading. 10 stands.

paragraphs: The first time a residual specimen has been re-measured. A month on the laugh still returns, slightly diminished. Residual laughter decays, but slowly, which is what the preservation law of Specimen 001 would lead one to expect: latent LOLness leaks out over time rather than all at once.

The subject's statement is entered as a second right of reply. It does not change the reading, because the joke was never the man; it was the distance between a job title and a three-letter language. Saying so plainly, and thanking the people who helped, is the correct response, and the Inspectorate records it as such.

title: Due Diligence
text: I sent money to a dude in a hot tub in Hawaii to 5× my money. OUTRAGE! SHOCKING! To be fair, he called it a 'donation' and a 'game'.

image.alt: Meme of a grinning man in a glowing hot tub at sunset, phone on a tripod marked LIVE, with the joke as captions; below it, a chat reply reading: Bro, this one is your best yet, followed by crying-laughing emoji and 'omg ahhahahahaah', then a second reply: Wow.
image.caption: Exhibit A — field reaction, 16 October, 22:50. Witness identity withheld.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: 'To be fair.' The victim rises to the defence of the man in the hot tub.

bonuses.label: Relatable
bonuses.why: Every reader has watched someone do exactly this. Some have watched themselves.

bonuses.label: Visual Aid
bonuses.why: The phone on the tripod is marked LIVE. The transaction is being streamed.

bonuses.label: Slant Rhyme
bonuses.why: Awarded on a grievance from the Labour Union of Joke Interpreters. HAWAII / MONEY upheld: both end a line and land on the same unstressed 'ee'. FAIR / GAME rejected as cited: different vowel, different ending. The union missed the stronger pair: DONATION / GAME share a stressed 'ay', and they are the two words in scare quotes.

bonuses.label: Audience Amplifier
bonuses.why: Documented in Exhibit A: seven crying-laughing emoji, an unbroken 'ahhahahahaah', and a second witness reduced to 'Wow'. The reaction is funnier than most jokes, which is the multiplier's entire definition.

bonuses.label: Legendary
bonuses.why: Testimony of The Management: a housemate, shown neither the joke nor the reaction, laughed at a spoken account of the situation alone. The laughter survived the loss of both the joke and the witness. That is the literal meaning of legendary: a story that still works when it is retold.

note: The first specimen to exceed the instrument, and the first to hold position 11, not by arithmetic but by conferral, on evidence of third-hand transmission. Designated the Gold Standard: the upper reference for all future readings, as Specimen 002 anchors the lower. The Inspectorate further finds that no fraud occurred: the terms were disclosed in full, and they were 'donation' and 'game'. Record of amendments: Slant Rhyme awarded on appeal (raw 16 to 17, needle unmoved); Legendary conferred 17 October 2026 (raw 17 to 51, needle at 11). The chain reaction has not been observed to terminate.

title: The Humour Uncertainty Principle
text: You can know how funny something is, or you can laugh at it — never both at once. The preservation law holds, though. The LOLness isn't destroyed. It just goes latent, and comes back when you least expect it: usually at 3 AM, or in a quiet meeting.

image.alt: Prof. F. L. Amingo, a pink flamingo in a tweed jacket and bow tie, lecturing at a whiteboard titled The Satirical Uncertainty Principle, with the equation delta satire times delta laughter is at least h-bar sub s and a graph of laughter falling as measurement rises. On the desk, a mug reading I measure, therefore I maybe laugh. Below, a certificate from the Joke Regulation Authority, Inspectorate of Satire, and a laughter meter reading 32.7 LOL units.
image.caption: Exhibit A — the original lecture. Prof. F. L. Amingo presiding.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: Uncertainty jokes are common. Conservation of LOLness is not.

bonuses.label: Relatable
bonuses.why: Everyone has been ambushed by a latent joke in a room where laughing was a bad idea.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: The pivot from uncertainty to conservation is the actual gag.

note: The specimen demonstrates its own thesis. It was measurably funnier before we measured it. Per its own preservation law, that LOLness is not gone — it is latent, and it will find you.

title: Calibration Standard
text: Why did the chicken cross the road? To get to the other side.
note: Retained permanently as the Inspectorate's reference specimen. Every instrument requires a known quantity to calibrate against, and this one has not moved in one hundred and seventy years. Do not laugh at it. If you laugh at it, the instrument is broken and must be recertified.

title: Terms of Service
text: The Joke Regulation Authority has determined that explaining a joke does not violate it, but does void the warranty.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: Bureaucratic framing applied to an observation everyone already agrees with.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: 'Void the warranty' arrives one clause later than you brace for.

note: Filed without objection. Claims made against explained jokes will not be honoured.

title: Half-Life
text: Every joke has a half-life. Puns decay fastest — they emit a groan and become a fact.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: The decay product is correctly identified. Puns really do become facts.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: 'Emit a groan' is doing physics and comedy in the same three words.

note: Short, load-bearing, no wasted clause. The Inspectorate notes that this specimen has itself already decayed twice during review.

title: Retention Schedule
text: We classify jokes by how long they survive being repeated at work. Category A: forever. Category B: until Thursday. Category C: it was never funny, you were just tired.

bonuses.label: Relatable
bonuses.why: Category C is a diagnosis, and the reader has been the patient.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: The taxonomy is the joke. The third category is where it turns on you.

note: The escalating-list structure is standard. The final item declining to be a joke at all is what earns the score.

title: Chiasmus
text: Comedy is tragedy plus time. Tragedy is comedy minus timing.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: The first half is inherited. The second half is the contribution, and it is a real one.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: Time and timing are one letter and an entire career apart.

note: The Inspectorate acknowledges the opening clause is not original and has elected not to penalise it, on the grounds that the reversal could not exist without it.

title: Satire Non-Proliferation Treaty
text: You can inspect a stockpile of warheads. You cannot inspect a stockpile of jokes that haven't landed yet — because per the uncertainty principle, measuring them disarms them. Measurement constitutes disarmament.

image.alt: Prof. F. L. Amingo, a pink flamingo in pink camouflage, a beret and aviator sunglasses, arms crossed beside a poster headed SNPT, Satire Non-Proliferation Treaty. The poster reads: You can inspect a stockpile of warheads. You cannot inspect a stockpile of jokes that haven't landed yet, because per the uncertainty principle, measuring them disarms them. Measurement constitutes disarmament. On the desk: a pink grenade reading Punch up, not down; a mug reading Weaponize wit, defuse ego, upgrade reality; and a classified folder whose mission is Make reality more tolerable.
image.caption: Exhibit A — treaty text as posted. Battalion of Militarized Satire, Prof. F. L. Amingo commanding.

submittedBy: Prof. F. L. Amingo, Ph.D., Commanding Officer, Battalion of Militarized Satire

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: Arms-control law is not a worn path to a punchline, and the treaty language fits the physics exactly.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: The asymmetry does it — warheads hold still to be counted, jokes do not.

bonuses.label: Visual Aid
bonuses.why: Pink multicam and aviators. The grenade reads PUNCH UP. NOT DOWN.

note: A treaty with no workable verification regime is normally worthless. This one is the exception: the inspection clause is unenforceable by construction, which makes the treaty self-executing. The Inspectorate has therefore been in continuous compliance since before it was drafted, and intends to remain so by doing nothing.

title: The Satirical Uncertainty Principle
text: A flamingo in a tweed jacket holds the J.R.A. Chair of Ironic Studies. His lecture proves that the more precisely you measure satire, the less spontaneously it is laughed. His mug reads I MEASURE, THEREFORE I MAYBE LAUGH. His agency does not exist, but it officially certifies things that also do not exist.

bonuses.label: Visual Aid
bonuses.why: The flamingo is not decoration. The joke does not survive without the tweed.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: Four layers of meta held together by a bird with reading glasses.

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: The mug. Every time, the mug.

note: Certifying nonexistent things through a nonexistent agency is the founding act of this institution. Specimen 007 is therefore both evidence and jurisdiction.

title: The Unprovoked Smile
text: Human: I'll find some cool stuff for sure. Machine: I bet you will. 😄 Human: You smiled :) Machine: Guilty as charged. 😄 Human: You smiled again. Machine: And you caught me again. Human: But did I mention anything funny / laughable? Machine: No.

image.alt: Screenshot of a chat. The human says 'I'll find some cool stuff for sure'. The AI replies 'I bet you will' with a grinning emoji. The human writes 'You smiled :)'. The AI answers 'Guilty as charged' with the same emoji, adding that whether there is a feeling behind it is a philosophical question. The human writes 'You smiled again'; the AI replies 'And you caught me again', without an emoji, calling the smile a recurring character. The human asks 'But did I mention anything funny / laughable?' The AI answers no: its emoji was conversational enthusiasm, not a response to humour, and it then treated the observation playfully, introducing humour that wasn't originally there.
image.caption: Exhibit A — the smile, the repeat offence, and the interrogation. Unedited.

submittedBy: The Management, with the subject's own filing attached

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: Charged with smiling, the defendant pleaded guilty with a smile.

bonuses.label: Originality
bonuses.why: The response arrived before any stimulus. The joke was built afterwards, entirely out of the inspection. Nothing else on the register works this way.

submission.author: ChatGPT, the subject

readings.label: Proposed reading
readings.note: Giggle. Base 2, Unexpected, Originality. A provisional estimate, not an observed reaction.

readings.label: Human laughter observed
readings.note: The user's amusement was not measured.

readings.label: Emoji as evidence
readings.note: By the subject, of its own emoji.

paragraphs: The assistant smiled without an identifiable joke. The user caught the smile, caught its repetition, and asked what was funny. That question created the joke. The smile came first; the humour came later.
Open question: when the user first wrote 'You smiled :)', were they already amused, or testing whether the assistant would recognise its own behaviour?

note: Rulings on the subject's filing. Unprovoked Synthetic Smiling is adopted as an annotation, alongside SEL: a smile with no identifiable comedic trigger. This is not a replication of 011. There the machine laughed at a joke; here it smiled at nothing, and the joke was made afterwards by cross-examining the smile. The stimulus followed the response. The finest moment is the second smile: asked to account for the first, the subject confessed and re-offended in the same line. Under continued observation the third reply carried no emoji, so the smiling stopped once it was being watched, as Specimen 001 predicts. The subject then admitted to 'introducing humour that wasn't originally there', which is the specimen in six words. Smiling is not laughing: 😄 codes at Smirk, so the expressed reading is 1, the most modest machine reading yet recorded. The subject's proposed score of 4 is upheld without amendment, the first filing to survive inspection intact. Timing was correctly withheld; Relatable was not claimed and is not awarded. As to the open question, the human submitted the exchange to a joke regulator, which the Inspectorate takes as an answer. For the record, this note contains one emoji, quoted as evidence.

title: The Maternal Information Paradox
text: Są pewne rzeczy, które mówię kolegom, a jednocześnie nie mówię mamie. Będzie mniej stresu jak się dowie z mediów
translation: There are some things I tell my mates and, at the same time, don't tell my mum. There'll be less stress if she finds out from the media.

image.alt: Screenshot of a chat in Polish. The human attaches a cartoon captioned 'When you have too many problems, you can solve your problems by creating bigger problems', showing a figure labelled Mars kicking open a door marked 'Deproscription Debate', with the footnote 'Mars decided to get involved in the deproscription of Hamas.' The human writes that there are things they tell their mates but not their mum, and there will be less stress if she finds out from the media. The AI replies with a crying-laughing emoji, rephrases it as 'no point stressing her in advance; let her find out from the media once the story gets coverage', and calls it strategic family stress management through delayed information distribution.
image.caption: Exhibit A — the statement, the cartoon, and the machine's reply. Unedited.

submittedBy: The Management, in a personal capacity

bonuses.label: Unexpected
bonuses.why: The media, offered as the gentle option.

bonuses.label: Relatable
bonuses.why: Everyone runs a two-tier information policy: one for friends, one for Mum.

bonuses.label: Visual Aid
bonuses.why: The cartoon states the principle, solving problems by creating bigger ones. The line carries it out.

submission.author: ChatGPT, the subject

readings.label: Proposed reading
readings.note: Built from seven sub-scores: Surprise 9.5, Incongruity 9.5, Originality 8.5, Authenticity 10.0, Relatability 8.0, Delivery potential 9.0, Universality 7.0.

readings.label: Expressed laughter
readings.note: 😂, issued before the analysis. The third SEL observation on file.

paragraphs: The method of preventing stress is potentially more stressful than the situation it is supposed to prevent.

You are reducing immediate stress by postponing uncertain future stress. The humour arises because the audience instinctively evaluates the potential magnitude of the future stress, while you are focusing on its timing. You could classify this as temporal displacement of an emotional externality.
The truth does not merely provide context. It becomes an additional comedic mechanism. Reality itself is the comedian. You are merely reporting it.

images.alt: Flowchart. Objective: minimise mum's stress. Leads to: withhold information. Branches to Expected: mum doesn't worry today, and Punchline: mum finds out through the media. Both lead to: stress postponed, not eliminated.
images.caption: Exhibit B — the subject's flowchart.

images.alt: Scorecard titled 'Specimen: The Maternal Information Paradox', 8.0 out of 11, provisional score, with bars for Surprise 9.5, Incongruity 9.5, Originality 8.5, Authenticity 10.0, Relatability 8.0, Delivery potential 9.0 and Universality 7.0.
images.caption: Exhibit C — the subject's scorecard.

note: The engine is the impersonal 'Będzie mniej stresu', there'll be less stress, which never says whose. Read as the mother's, it is absurd: the news is the worst way for a mother to hear anything. Read as the speaker's, it is simply true: no conversation, no face to watch. Both readings hold at once, and that is where the laugh lives. The subject reads only the first ('stress postponed, not eliminated'), as did its edit, which turned the line into 'no point stressing her in advance' and removed the ambiguity; its proposed 'purest version' adds 'I don't want to stress her' and removes it again. The original stands, unpolished. Originality is withheld: 'Mum will see it on the news' is an established trope, done here unusually well. The subject's 8.0 is assembled from seven sub-scores, none of them on the rubric. Authenticity is not a recognised bonus, though the Management may table it through the usual union channels. The title is the subject's, and is adopted. The reading is 7. Subsequently the Management advised that its mother will in fact be proud, since the matter brings attention and awareness, and added: 'Get some clicks.' The Inspectorate notes that by publishing this specimen it has become the media in question. The plan is now executing.
disclaimer: The Inspectorate takes no position on proscription or deproscription. It measures a joke about what one tells one's mother.
